blocks.text: 1. The Forget Gate

blocks.alt: The previous hidden state and current input feed the forget gate to produce a forget decision

blocks.text: LSTM Architecture, the previous topic, introduced three gates managing the cell state. The Forget Gate gives a complete, dedicated look at LSTM's first gate, explored in full depth throughout this topic.
It decides what information to genuinely discard from the cell state, a genuinely important, foundational mechanism covered throughout the rest of this topic.
2. Recapping The Preview

This connects back to the quick preview of all three gates, already covered in LSTM Architecture. The forget gate was genuinely introduced there as the first of three gates, briefly described in that earlier topic.
This topic genuinely gives it the complete, dedicated treatment already promised, exploring every mathematical and practical detail already hinted at throughout LSTM Architecture.
3. What The Forget Gate Takes As Input

blocks.alt: The previous hidden state combines with the current input

blocks.text: This connects back to the core idea, already covered in Vanilla RNN. The forget gate genuinely looks at the current input and the genuinely previous hidden state, gathering the same information available at every time step.
This is the exact same two ingredients already covered as Vanilla RNN's own core update rule, reused here as the genuinely raw material the forget gate uses to make its own decision.

blocks.text: 4. Interpreting The Output

blocks.alt: An output near 0 means forget while an output near 1 means keep

blocks.text: This connects back to the Sigmoid gating mechanism, already covered in LSTM Architecture. The forget gate genuinely outputs a value between 0 and 1 for each element of the cell state.
A genuine 0 means genuinely forget that piece of information entirely; a genuine 1 means genuinely keep it entirely, giving a genuinely smooth, fine-grained range of choices in between as well.
5. Applying The Gate

blocks.alt: A forget gate value multiplies the old cell state to produce a filtered cell state

blocks.text: The genuinely core operation connects back to the cell state idea, already covered in LSTM Architecture. Multiply the genuinely previous cell state, element by element, by the forget gate's own output.
This genuinely direct multiplication, already covered in this section, is exactly how the forget gate's own decision, already covered in the previous section, actually takes effect on the cell state.
6. Learned Forgetting

blocks.alt: The forget gate is learned during training

blocks.text: This connects back to filters being genuinely learned, already covered in Filters and Kernels. The forget gate's own weights are genuinely learned through training, exactly like any other weight in the network.
The network genuinely learns for itself what information is safe to discard at each step, rather than following any genuinely fixed, hand-designed forgetting rule.

blocks.title: info
blocks.content: This learned forgetting, already covered in this topic, is a genuinely important reason LSTMs can adapt their own memory management to genuinely different tasks, rather than relying on one single, universal forgetting strategy.

blocks.text: 7. Why Forgetting Is Genuinely Useful

A genuinely important, real practical insight connects back to the compression limit, already covered in Hidden State. Selectively forgetting genuinely irrelevant information frees up genuinely valuable capacity for what actually matters.

This directly helps manage the fixed-size capacity limit already covered in that earlier topic, letting the network genuinely prioritize the most currently relevant information instead of trying to retain everything at once.
8. A Practical Initialization Detail

A genuinely important, real practical detail connects back to Weight Initialization, already covered in its own module. The forget gate's own bias is genuinely often initialized to encourage remembering by default at the very start of training.

This mirrors the deliberate, careful choices already covered throughout that earlier module, applied here specifically to help early training avoid genuinely forgetting everything before the network has learned anything useful.

blocks.text: 9. Recognizing Why The Forget Gate Is Genuinely Essential

blocks.alt: Needing to drop stale information points toward the forget gate

blocks.text: This connects back to genuinely long sequences with genuinely shifting relevant context. The forget gate, already covered in this topic, directly lets the network drop genuinely outdated information.

This connects back to the cell state idea, already covered in LSTM Architecture, needing active management. The forget gate, already covered, is genuinely the first, essential piece of that active management.
10. Worked Example

The example below directly demonstrates the forget gate's own effect on a cell state, contrasting a mostly-forgetting gate against a mostly-keeping gate, illustrating the concepts already covered throughout this topic.

code.content:
import numpy as np

def sigmoid(x):
    return 1 / (1 + np.exp(-x))

previous_cell_state = np.array([2.5, -1.3, 0.8, 4.0])  # already covered as the cell state idea in this topic

# already covered as interpreting the output in this topic
mostly_forgetting_gate = sigmoid(np.array([-3.0, -3.0, -3.0, -3.0]))  # close to 0
mostly_keeping_gate = sigmoid(np.array([3.0, 3.0, 3.0, 3.0]))          # close to 1

after_forgetting = previous_cell_state * mostly_forgetting_gate  # already covered as applying the gate in this topic
after_keeping = previous_cell_state * mostly_keeping_gate

print("Previous cell state:", previous_cell_state)
print(f"Forget gate values (mostly forgetting): {np.round(mostly_forgetting_gate, 3)}")
print(f"Cell state after mostly forgetting: {np.round(after_forgetting, 3)}")
print(f"\nForget gate values (mostly keeping): {np.round(mostly_keeping_gate, 3)}")
print(f"Cell state after mostly keeping: {np.round(after_keeping, 3)}")

blocks.title: info
blocks.content: Running this example shows the same original cell state shrinking dramatically under a mostly-forgetting gate, while staying nearly unchanged under a mostly-keeping gate, exactly the effect already covered as applying the gate in this topic.

blocks.text: 11. Key Takeaways

items: The forget gate decides what information to discard from the cell state.
It takes the current input and the previous hidden state as its own input, like Vanilla RNN's update rule.
It outputs a value between 0 and 1 per cell state element, using Sigmoid.
This output gets multiplied element-wise into the previous cell state to apply the gate.
Its weights are learned through training, letting the network learn what to forget for itself.
Selective forgetting frees up capacity for genuinely relevant, current information.
Its bias is often initialized to favor remembering at the very start of training.
It is the first, essential piece of actively managing the cell state.
Next up: The Input Gate, deciding what new information to add to the cell state.
